segments.text: Some prophecies predict disasters. This one predicts something that looks, from the outside... like success. Golden domes. Record-breaking minarets. And a warning hiding inside the glitter.
segments._shot: ornate golden dome gleaming at sunset, exterior only

segments.text: This is the sign... of the boast.
segments.title: THE BOAST
segments._shot: slow gold filigree light patterns on black

segments.text: A mosque... masjid in Arabic... is simply a place of prostration, where Muslims pray. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, prayed in one built of mud brick and palm trunks, with a roof that leaked when it rained. From inside that simplicity... he saw what was coming.
segments._shot: mud-brick fort walkway in warm sunset light

segments.text: The Hour will not be established... he said... until people boast about their mosques. Narrated by his servant Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him... recorded in Sunan Abi Dawud, and graded authentic.
segments._shot: towering ornate minarets, low dramatic angle

segments.text: Another collection carries the same warning with one sharper word... people will show off in building mosques. The building is not the sign... the showing off is. My dome against your dome. My city's skyline against yours.
segments._shot: glittering chandeliers and gilded ceiling, tilt-up

segments.text: The precision matters. Building mosques is beloved in Islam... the Prophet, peace be upon him, promised a house in Paradise for it. The sign is not the marble. It is the motive... when houses built for humility become monuments to pride, while the prayer rows inside them thin out.
segments._shot: vast empty prayer hall, beams of light, no people

segments.text: He worshipped under a leaking roof and changed the world. The prophecy asks a question every generation answers for itself... is the beauty for Allah... or for the photograph?
segments._shot: empty old stone mosque corner, warm lantern light
